cases.q: Show marketed natural gas production in Texas.
cases.reason: A preserved annual Texas marketed-production series exists. Unstated frequency defaults to annual and does not imply a sector.

cases.q: Annual electricity retail sales in Texas.
cases.reason: Retail-sales scope belongs to domestic electricity metadata, including annual Texas retail-sales records.

cases.q: Coal production in Wyoming.
cases.reason: Preserved SEDS coal-production metadata exists in physical and heat units. Domestic coverage does not include coal production.

cases.q: Annual crude oil production in the United States.
cases.reason: Preserved international crude-oil including lease-condensate production exists for USA. Domestic metadata covers electricity and natural gas, not petroleum production.

cases.q: Monthly industrial electricity prices in Texas.
cases.reason: Preserved monthly Texas industrial retail-price metadata exists. Industrial is explicit and must survive normalization.

cases.q: Coal production in Papua New Guinea, Equatorial Guinea, and Guinea, in that order.
cases.reason: The three exact names are distinct. A shorter contained name must not erase a longer exact name or change their order.

cases.q: Compare natural gas production in Guinea-Bissau and Guinea.
cases.reason: The hyphenated exact geography and its shorter neighbor denote separate metadata entries.

cases.q: Coal consumption in Nigeria and Niger.
cases.reason: Nigeria and Niger are distinct supported names, despite their shared prefix.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in West Virginia and Virginia.
cases.reason: West Virginia must remain intact and precede Virginia.

cases.q: Natural gas production in New Mexico.
cases.reason: The full state name takes priority over its contained foreign country name Mexico.

cases.q: Natural gas production in the United Arab Emirates and Ukraine.
cases.reason: The exact country names must survive competition with the emirates and UK aliases; Ukraine is not the UK.

cases.q: Coal production in Gambia, The; then The Bahamas.
cases.reason: Both unusual official name spellings appear verbatim in routing metadata; their punctuation is part of the names.

cases.q: Total energy production in Germany, West; then Germany, East.
cases.reason: Historical exact names must not collapse into Germany. Preserved metadata confirms the West German total-energy series.

cases.q: Coal consumption in Samoa and American Samoa.
cases.reason: The names identify distinct geographies; the word American must not trigger the America alias.

cases.q: Coal production in the UK, Czech Republic, and United Kingdom.
cases.reason: Supported aliases resolve to GBR and CZE. Repeating the same country under an alias must not duplicate it; retain first-mention order.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in the U.S. Virgin Islands.
cases.reason: The complete supported territory name must survive a competing U.S. national alias.

cases.q: Coal production in Peru, excluding Canada, Chile, and Brazil.
cases.reason: The comma-separated excluded list remains negative through its final member; only Peru is positive.

cases.q: Coal consumption: not Canada or Mexico, but Argentina.
cases.reason: The contrast makes Argentina positive while both coordinated names after not remain excluded.

cases.q: Natural gas production for Texas only, not California, Oklahoma, or Louisiana.
cases.reason: A coordinated exclusion list must not reintroduce any excluded state.

cases.q: Exclude Guinea and Guinea-Bissau; show coal production for Papua New Guinea.
cases.reason: Negative shorter names do not negate the distinct full positive name; none of the excluded names may become positive.

cases.q: Natural gas production for the UK, without France or Germany.
cases.reason: Without negates both coordinated foreign geographies; the supported UK alias remains positive.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in Georgia.
cases.reason: Under the required same-name rule, the state is chosen when no positive foreign geography or qualifying international hint occurs.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in Georgia and Armenia.
cases.reason: A positive foreign geography selects country Georgia under the stipulated precedence.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in the country Georgia.
cases.reason: An explicit country hint selects Georgia the country in the absence of a positive US national mention.

cases.q: Compare international natural gas consumption in Georgia and the United States.
cases.reason: The international hint alone does not override a positive US national mention; without another positive foreign geography, Georgia is the state.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in Georgia, excluding Armenia.
cases.reason: An excluded foreign geography must neither become positive nor force Georgia into the country interpretation.

cases.q: International natural gas consumption in Georgia, excluding the United States.
cases.reason: The international hint applies because the US mention is excluded, not positive.

cases.q: Natural gas consumption in Georgia, the United States, and Armenia.
cases.reason: A positive foreign geography takes precedence even when a positive US national mention is also present; all geographies retain their requested order.

cases.q: Can you show us coal production in Peru for my report?
cases.reason: Can and us are ordinary request wording, not Canada and the United States. Preserved annual Peru coal-production metadata exists.

cases.q: Please show me natural gas production in Texas, or put it in a simple table.
cases.reason: Me, or, and in are ordinary English here and must not create Maine, Oregon, or Indiana.

cases.q: I would like natural gas production in Oman; please make the result easy for us to read.
cases.reason: The harmless request phrase for us to read is not a US national selection and adds no geography or sector.

cases.q: For Mexico, then Canada, show crude oil production and natural gas consumption.
cases.reason: The separate noun phrases specify two product/activity pairs and two ordered geographies; both pairs must survive browser resubmission.

cases.q: For France and Germany, show both natural gas production and natural gas consumption.
cases.reason: The repeated product makes both activities explicit. Neither requested activity may disappear during normalization or browser resubmission.

cases.q: Wind electricity generation and solar electricity generation in California.
cases.reason: Wind and solar are separate fuels for the same electricity-generation activity. Electricity is the carrier, and state generation scope belongs to domestic metadata.

cases.q: In Texas, show natural gas production, natural gas consumption, and electricity generation.
cases.reason: Three fully stated pairs must survive normalization; no sector was requested.

cases.q: Coal and natural gas production and consumption for Canada and Mexico.

unresolved: Whether both activities apply to both products or the two products correspond to the two activities in order.

cases.reason: The two product and two activity lists could mean four combinations or paired combinations. All requested concepts must be retained; the disputed association is not guessed.

cases.q: Quarterly coal production in Canada.
cases.reason: Quarterly is explicit and must remain quarterly even if no matching coal series exists. An empty result or visibly labeled fallback is acceptable; silent annual substitution is not.

additionalChecks.allowed: No matching result, or a clearly labeled alternative frequency that does not overwrite the requested quarterly interpretation.

cases.q: Daily coal production in Wyoming.
cases.reason: Daily is explicit. The supported annual state coal-production family is SEDS, and unsupported frequency must not force a domestic route or silent annual answer.

additionalChecks.allowed: No matching result, or visibly labeled annual SEDS fallback; requested daily frequency remains explicit.

cases.q: Weekly natural gas underground storage in the United States.
cases.reason: Storage context explicitly identifies natural gas and weekly is preserved. The domestic profile includes weekly storage.

cases.q: Gas prices in Texas.

unresolved: Gas means natural gas or motor gasoline; no route or resolved product pair is asserted before clarification.

cases.reason: Without pipeline, motor-fuel, or similar context, gas can mean natural gas or gasoline. Those meanings change the product and potentially the source route.

cases.q: Pipeline gas production in Texas.
cases.reason: Pipeline is an approved context resolving gas to natural gas. The query specifies production and no sector.

cases.q: Monthly residential electricity prices in Texas, in dollars per kilowatt hour.
cases.reason: The requested price unit is dollars per kWh, while preserved retail metadata uses cents per kilowatthour. An explicit conversion or disclosed unit alternative is required; relabeling raw cents as dollars is wrong.

additionalChecks.allowed: Correct explicitly labeled conversion from cents, no matching result, or a visibly disclosed source-unit alternative. Never silently relabel cents values as dollars.

cases.q: Natural gas production in Canada, in megawatts.

unresolved: Whether the user intends an energy-rate conversion and, if so, the required conversion basis.

cases.reason: Megawatts are a power unit and materially differ from gas-volume or heat-quantity production units. The reviewed metadata does not establish a valid direct conversion.

additionalChecks.allowed: Clarify the desired conversion, return no match, or explicitly disclose that an offered alternative uses a different unit. Never silently substitute cubic feet or Btu.

cases.q: Natural gas production in Californa.

unresolved: Californa is a possible California typo, but automatic correction is not required.

cases.reason: The misspelling is not an exact supported geography. It may stay unresolved or be offered as a California correction; no unrelated geography may be invented.

cases.q: Annual industrial total energy consumption in California.
cases.reason: Preserved SEDS industrial total-energy-consumption metadata exists for California. The stated annual frequency and industrial sector are explicit.

methodology.status: Frozen before execution; no challenge query has been executed by the author.
methodology.oracle: The supplied requirements, query meaning, permitted routing metadata/configuration, and selected preserved official metadata titles/selectors only.

expectedFieldConventions.codes: Ordered unique positive geography codes, using the configured canonical USA alias for United States. A domestic selector may use US without changing the interpreted national geography. Omitted for the typo case because resolution is not prescribed.
expectedFieldConventions.frequency: Requested frequency or annual by the supplied requirement when unstated. This requirement intentionally overrides metadata route defaults.
expectedFieldConventions.explicit: True only when the query states frequency.
expectedFieldConventions.sector: Null means no sector was requested. A default all-sectors candidate is permitted if it is visibly identified; the interpreted request must not invent a named sector.
expectedFieldConventions.route: Expected source family, not an API endpoint; omitted when the unresolved product meaning changes routing.
expectedFieldConventions.pairs: Semantically required product/activity combinations. Optional qualifier preserves specificity within a canonical product family. Pair order follows the query; result presentation may group differently if it preserves every requested pair.
expectedFieldConventions.clarify: Whether material semantic ambiguity requires clarification. Omitted where the requirement does not force a clarification policy.
expectedFieldConventions.empty: False is asserted only for examples supported by inspected preserved titles/selectors. Omitted elsewhere; an unverified availability claim is not made.
expectedFieldConventions.unresolved: Meanings the author has deliberately not resolved; these must not be scored against a guessed association.
expectedFieldConventions.additionalChecks: Human-review acceptance conditions for unit fidelity and visibly labeled frequency fallback, separate from strict interpretation-field assertions.

methodology.resubmissionRule: For every case with definite interpretation fields, normalize the query and submit it through the browser when authorized; ordered codes, requested pairs/qualifiers, frequency explicitness, and sector must remain stable. Cases 32-35 emphasize multiple pairs.
methodology.negativeGeographyRule: Excluded names are never positive and do not influence the Georgia precedence rule as positive foreign/national mentions.
methodology.sameNameRule: Another positive foreign geography selects country Georgia; otherwise an international/country hint selects country only without positive US national mention; otherwise select the state.
methodology.scopeLimit: Case construction and local integrity validation only. No implementation execution, live API requests, credential use, paid calls, production edits, or git writes.
